events.title: The first capping at Àth leathan
events.body: In am Màrt An seachdamh rèisimeid pours the first concrete over a flooded shaft at Àth leathan while Somhairle mac Lachlainn watches from the pit-head; the mix lies still in a way the seam itself, even flooded, had never once lain before.

events.title: Sergeant Iain Mòr counts the cappings
events.body: A sergeant of An seachdamh rèisimeid tells Somhairle mac Lachlainn this is the fourth capping his company has stood by that month, at Muileann àrsaidh, Cnoc thais and a nameless working near Àth naomh, and wonders aloud what the regiment will be set to guard once Tobar dhearg of the hills is done.

events.title: Comhairle nam Mèinnean ends the coal trade outside An Sloc Mòr
events.body: Fearghas mac Aonghais's office notes that the trade in coal-fuel is at an end on the island outside what Comhairle nam Mèinnean still cuts for its own account at An Sloc Mòr: not forbidden by any law, but ended by there being, at last, nowhere left to sell it.

events.title: Aonghas mac Phàdraig's plough finds the first iron
events.body: Turning his field at Muileann ghlas in am Màrt as he has every spring of his life, Aonghas mac Phàdraig's share brings up a rusted bayonet lying whole across it; he finishes the furrow before he carries it home.

events.title: A' chiad rèisimeid's corporal begins a list
events.body: A corporal of A' chiad rèisimeid collecting rents in the district takes Aonghas mac Phàdraig's bayonet and enters it on a list kept for such finds, not knowing whether it is a record of the dead or only of the field giving back what two armies left in it.

events.title: The letter from the capital's gaol
events.body: Martha Greaves receives word from the council's office that the holdouts taken at Muileann ghlas are to be released in an t-Iuchar and marched north to the boundary stones, with no word of who is to feed them on the road or what their flooded towns will make of their return.

events.title: Martha Greaves and Peter Hale ride to the stones
events.body: Martha Greaves and Peter Hale take the last carriage Slighe a' Ghuail runs toward the boundary stones, Peter carrying a register freshly ruled with a new column by his own hand for want of any other paper the party trusted.

events.title: A mother writes four words beside her son's name
events.body: A woman of Cnoc thais gives Martha Greaves her son's name for the register and, unbidden, the words he is not among these; Martha sets both down, judging the register poorer without them.

events.title: A man refuses his name for a town that no longer stands
events.body: An older prisoner at the boundary stones will not give his name at first, saying it would mean nothing written beside Muileann àrsaidh's ruin; Martha Greaves promises the town will stand again in whatever shape its people build it, and he gives his name.

events.title: Peter Hale keeps a name of his own
events.body: Among the released Peter Hale recognises a man once apprenticed to the same binder at Muileann leathan whose pupils rebound Tional nan Tuathach's minute-books; the man gives no sign of knowing him, and Peter does not ask which it is, silence or forgetting.

events.title: Anna nic Phàil speaks to Somhairle at the chamber door
events.body: At the close of his first sitting Anna nic Phàil tells Somhairle mac Lachlainn she stood on the bench in the passage an Nollaig Martha Greaves carried Athchuinge Dheireannach an Tionail in, and means to go on voting every mercy the council's business allows her.

events.title: Somhairle reads the one-and-sixty names
events.body: At the stone's unveiling at Cathair mhòr, Somhairle mac Lachlainn reads aloud the one-and-sixty names of the regiments' dead from Àth leathan and Muileann ghlas to a silent square, and finds the town's silence harder to bear than any noise it might have made instead.

events.title: Somhairle thinks of the names the stone does not carry
events.body: Standing alone at the stone after the crowd disperses, Somhairle mac Lachlainn counts over the column's uncounted dead, the sixty from the byres, and a mother's son who was not among the released, and finds that number, cut nowhere, stays with him longer than the one that is.

events.title: Four score released at the boundary stones
events.body: Some four score holdouts taken at Muileann ghlas are handed to Tional nan Tuathach at the boundary stones; Martha Greaves writes their names in a column Peter Hale ruled that morning.

events.title: The heading on Clach nan Rèisimeidean
events.body: Clach nan Rèisimeidean is cut in two columns under a single heading, the regiments' dead, giving neither battle nor date.

events.title: Two brothers of Seann Bhral on the stone
events.body: Among the names read at the stone's unveiling are two brothers of Seann Bhral who enlisted together and died within the same hour of the same morning.

events.title: An seachdamh rèisimeid's first winter at the post
events.body: An seachdamh rèisimeid's first winter at the post by Àth leathan is spent roofing it; the men buy their slates at the western Seann Skell.

events.title: The first market under the Caol ruadh charter
events.body: The first market held under Caol ruadh's new charter is held in the rain on the quay; the market-due is taken by a clerk of An t-Ionmhas under a sailcloth awning, and the fishwives sell out before noon.

events.title: A plough-share of Muileann ghlas
events.body: The farmer of the sown field at Muileann ghlas brings the first blade turned up by his plough to the regiments' post, and the corporal enters it in a book kept for the purpose.

events.title: The council's order reaches Muileann chaol
events.body: A rider who has changed horses three times brings the council's four-line order to Raghnall mac Mhuirich on the doorstep of the old building: the whole record of An Cogadh Fada is to be shut against every reader for fifty years, and the keeper alone is to hold the key.

events.title: Raghnall has a room built for the seal
events.body: Raghnall clears an old storeroom at the end of the new wing's gallery and has a mason and a smith fit it, through a fortnight of hard weather, with an oak door two inches thick and a lock made new to no other key in the kingdom, standing over the last morning's fitting himself.

events.title: Sìleas carries her full record to the door
events.body: Over two days Sìleas nic Rath carries her own four boxes of the war's full record up from her room and sets them inside the new door herself, letting no clerk touch them: the movements, counts and letters she was never let publish alongside the open chronicle.

events.title: The key turns once
events.body: Raghnall turns the new lock himself with the mason and smith gone, and hangs the key on a cord under his own shirt, where he is seen for years after to lay his hand against his chest before he blows out the reading-room's last lamp.

events.title: Sìleas's promise at the head of the open list
events.body: Sìleas writes, unasked, a line at the head of the war's open list saying plainly that the fuller record exists, is kept, and will be given to any honest reader when the fifty years end; Raghnall reads it and lets it stand.

events.title: An seachdamh rèisimeid's captain lets the cairn stand
events.body: Asked whether to clear the cairn the Tuathaich have raised on Àraich Àth leathan, Comhairle nam Mèinnean answers that its captain may use his own judgment; he tells his patrols to walk past it and count the stones if they wish, and report only what is found beneath one.

events.title: A woman of Àth leathan carries a stone each morning
events.body: A woman of the town who lost a brother in the fighting there, and will not say which side he died fighting for, is seen to walk out alone before the patrol each morning, set one stone on the cairn, and stand a while with her hand flat against it before going home.

events.title: Peigi nic Ascaill signs the regiments' contract
events.body: Peigi nic Ascaill signs Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail' contract for the regiments' engines and the fleets' hulls at Cathair dhearg with a clerk on either hand to witness it, and tells her under-fitter afterward that no paper she has signed will put more Dia-thìrich fitters to the trade than this one.

events.title: A smith of Àth naomh counts his musket-stocks
events.body: Writing to his brother at Cathair dhearg, a smith of Àth naomh says he has turned out more musket-stocks that winter than ploughshares in the six years before the war, and cannot decide whether to call it his own good fortune or the kingdom's bad one.

events.title: The forge at Caol ìseal takes on new hands
events.body: The woman who masters the forge at Caol ìseal, left her by a father with no son to leave it to, takes on four boys and a girl under the arms contract and tells Comhairle nam Mèinnean's inspector she means to keep them past the contract's term, war or no war.

events.title: Seonag nic Thòmais lights the second lamp
events.body: Keeper of the trial lamp at Baile ìseal, Seonag nic Thòmais sees the salt-boat raiders' sail two hours before An dàrna cabhlach's own lookout and lights, on her own judgment, the warning lamp kept unlit in ordinary weather; the fleet's captain copies her log whole into his return.

events.title: Sìleas opens the next day's page as any other
events.body: The morning after the lock is turned, Sìleas sets the day's date and the weather at the top of her page and writes only of a mill's copying fee, exactly as on any working morning of the thirteen years before, and says nothing there of the sealed room.

events.title: Some forty places on the open list
events.body: The open list of the war years at an Leabharlann runs to some forty places, each with its regiments and the counts allowed before the sealing, and a blank where the column's dead would stand.

events.title: The quays of Baile ghorm lengthened
events.body: For An treas cabhlach's tank-hulls the quays of Baile ghorm are lengthened by forty paces into the anchorage, the stone carted from the old wolf-posts' quarry.

events.title: Doire shean pays the market-due
events.body: At Doire shean the fixed market-due is taken for the first time; Am Buabhall Fortanach, which sells no goods at market, is found to owe it on its buffalo.

events.title: Còmhrag Ceann leathan of Ceann leathan after the war
events.body: At the first Còmhrag at Ceann leathan after the last pits gave up, the fair-wardens count more fighters from the shires of the middle country than in any year before, and none from the western hills.

events.title: Anna nic Phàil cuts a page of figures from her own draft
events.body: Writing her motion at her own table through the early months of the year, Anna nic Phàil cuts a whole page of named costs, granaries and flooded pit-heads and Clach nan Rèisimeidean, judging that a council grows deaf to a column of figures faster than to almost anything else brought before it.

events.title: The master of An t-Ionmhas asks a figure of the motion
events.body: Uisdean Dubh, master of An t-Ionmhas, asks Anna nic Phàil's Tagradh na h-Èirig whether its sum has been costed against the year's roll; she answers that the reckoning is the room's own trade, and asks only that the principle be granted.

events.title: The motion held over, morning after morning
events.body: For eight sittings running the council's clerk carries Tagradh na h-Èirig forward on the day's business-paper under the same two words, held over, without any member speaking against it or any vote being called.

events.title: Somhairle mac Lachlainn is asked whether the sum is too great
events.body: Caught at the chamber door, Somhairle mac Lachlainn tells Anna nic Phàil that he has read many rolls of the dead and never once been asked whether the towns that raised them could bear the cost, and does not know why a roll of the dead should be easier to pay for than a roll of the living.

events.title: The motion stood over without a sitting called
events.body: On the eighth day Tagradh na h-Èirig is absent from the business-paper; a clerk tells Anna nic Phàil it was stood over to the autumn sitting the evening before, in a short session she was not told was sitting, by members' vote without her among them.

events.title: Anna counts the councillors who looked away
events.body: Going back over the eight sittings, Anna nic Phàil can find no single vote that killed the motion, only the faces of the twelve, one who promised a vote and never called it, one who spoke of hard times, six who said nothing to her at all, and Somhairle who gave her an answer and moved no more than the rest to call it to a vote.

events.title: Martha Greaves tells Peter Hale she means to lay the chair down
events.body: In the delegates' room over the net-lofts at Caol mhòr, Martha Greaves tells Peter Hale plainly that she means to lay down Tional nan Tuathach's chair that year, and that she judges him, of every delegate she has sat among, the fittest to take it up.

events.title: Martha Greaves's last sitting
events.body: Martha Greaves reads out the year's register and the ordinary business of the day, a roof at the school, the price of wool, a mill's complaint of the coal-line's freight, lays the chair down, and Tional nan Tuathach chooses Peter Hale by acclamation without a show of hands.

events.title: Martha Greaves goes home to Doire ghlas
events.body: Martha Greaves rides home to Doire ghlas on the ordinary carrier's cart with no more baggage than she came to the mill with as a young woman, not yet certain what a woman who was Tional nan Tuathach's own voice for seventeen years is to do with her mornings now.

events.title: Officers' houses at Inis uaine
events.body: By council order An t-ochdamh rèisimeid's officers at Inis uaine are given houses in the town in place of quarters borrowed year by year from the tank-yard's sheds.

events.title: The quarrymen of Seann Warr
events.body: The quarrymen of Seann Warr cut the stone for An còigeamh rèisimeid's barracks through the summer from the same face that gave the harbour wall, and are paid by An t-Ionmhas at a rate the town's masons call fair.

events.title: Cnoc bhàn's harbour opened again
events.body: The Tuathaich of Cnoc bhàn open their harbour again to boats they do not know, the raiders who took the salt-boats having been brought into Seann Skell.

events.title: The springs of Muileann ruadh in a wet summer
events.body: Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh below Muileann ruadh run so full in the wet summer that the bath-house's lower room floods, and the custodians carry the sick up to the long room.
